newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel - low sulphur takes breather after deals.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel - low sulphur takes breather after deals.

text.p: NWE low sulphur cracked fuel was steady on Friday after 100,000 tonnes was sold yesterday.
A 45-50,000 tonne cargo was sold on Thursday and two handysize cargoes were also done, one at $124 fob Denmark. The other deals were private, but the large parcel was rumoured at around $125.75 fob.
A 25kt cargo was offered today at $125 fob ex Scandinavia while a 45-50kt parcel was being put together in the U.K.
Business was not expected to pick up."We might see a couple of trades next week..people hoping to pick up a bargin, but otherwise it should be quiet," said one oil major trader.
The high sulphur cracked market looked very quiet although there was a rumour that 50kt was done for Romania.

"Nothing's happened as far as I can see, its pretty much a dead market," said one dealer. Trades have been few and far between in recent weeks and some traders feel prices will weaken from their current level of $115 cif NWE.
High sulphur barge activity was slowish with $118 fob ARA a tonne done for Jan barrels. Bunker demand was fair, but prices balanced by good supplies and strong competition
